summary: This FYI memo is a short bibliography of recent resources to help a network novice learn about the Internet, including its networks, resources, protocols, and history. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 1463 is a short reading list for people who are new to the Internet. It groups books and papers by subject and explains how to get the items that were available online at no charge.

questions: how do beginners learn about the internet
subtitle: A short 1993 bibliography for people learning about the Internet and its protocols.

tldr.problem: People new to the Internet may need help finding introductory information about networks, services, resources, protocols, and history.
tldr.mechanism: This FYI memo groups books and papers by topic and marks items that were available online at no charge. It also explains how to obtain those online files.
tldr.outcome: RFC 1463 is a brief bibliography intended for use as a handout by user services personnel. It recommends asking a network service provider for further information.

sections.title: A Reading List for New Internet Users
sections.content:
RFC 1463 offers a short list of recent information resources for people new to the Internet. It covers the Internet, related networks, resources, protocols, and history. The memo is intentionally brief so user services personnel can use it as a handout.

The bibliography includes both free online sources and traditional publications. It advises readers with further questions to contact their network service provider, and points people interested in connectivity to books that help locate a provider.
sections.plainLanguage: The memo helps a new Internet user choose introductory books and papers. It also points readers to their network service provider for more help.

sections.title: Topics Covered by the Bibliography
sections.content:
The list covers introductory papers and books, guides to getting connected, Internet services and resources, Internet networks, and Internet protocols. It also includes further reading for people who want more detail. Items marked with an asterisk were available online at no charge according to the memo.

The examples include introductory guides, books about Internet use, directories, and technical books on TCP/IP. The RFC is a bibliography, not a tutorial that explains those topics itself.
sections.plainLanguage: The reading list includes beginner guides, information on getting connected, network directories, and technical material about protocols. An asterisk identifies resources the memo says were free online.

sections.title: How the Memo Says to Get Online Materials
sections.content:
The final section explains how readers with Internet access could obtain the online documents marked with an asterisk. It provides an email address for requesting an access guide and lists anonymous FTP sites where the guide could be retrieved. The guide also describes obtaining documents through dial-up service using a modem for people without direct Internet access.

The memo notes that network providers may publish additional user guides and newsletters. It also points readers who need a more comprehensive bibliography to RFC 1175.
sections.plainLanguage: The memo explains how to request or download the access guide for free online materials. It also describes a dial-up option for readers without direct Internet access.
